followed the clinical course of a previously healthy 44-year-
old Caucasian woman for 6 months. She presented with sub-

acute onset of double vision and leg spasm for 4 weeks until
she was unable to move her eyes or walk. Ophthalmological
examination revealed complete ophthalmoplegia but normal
visual acuity and optic disc. Neurological examination dem-
onstrated severe spasticity and hyperreflexia in her legs, spar-
ing her arms. She could not walk because of pain and stiff-
ness. The rest of her examination was unremarkable. Her
workup revealed a mediastinal mass and a markedly elevated
anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (anti-GAD) antibody titer.
